PHB racial ability limits below show each ability as minimum–maximum. A maximum written M/F gives the male maximum first and female maximum second; otherwise both are the same. Apply racial adjustments before the maximum; qualifying minimums can include an applicable racial bonus.
Dwarf: Strength 8–18/17; Intelligence 3–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 3–17; Constitution 12–19; Charisma 3–16.
Elf: Strength 3–18/16; Intelligence 8–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 7–19; Constitution 6–18; Charisma 8–18.
Gnome: Strength 6–18/15; Intelligence 7–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 3–18; Constitution 8–18; Charisma 3–18.
Half-elf: Strength 3–18/17; Intelligence 4–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 6–18; Constitution 6–18; Charisma 3–18.
Halfling: Strength 6–17/14; Intelligence 6–18; Wisdom 3–17; Dexterity 8–18; Constitution 10–19; Charisma 3–18.
Half-orc: Strength 6–18; Intelligence 3–17; Wisdom 3–14; Dexterity 3–17; Constitution 13–19; Charisma 3–12.

The PHB notes that fighters of all races might qualify for exceptional Strength; see the Strength table. This table covers the six listed nonhuman and part-human races; class requirements remain separate.
The dwarf Charisma maximum applies with respect to non-dwarves; the half-orc maximum applies with respect to non-orcs and non-half-orcs (PHB p.13).

oldValue: Gray elves share high-elf abilities, including sleep and charm resistance, sword and bow ability, infravision, secret/concealed-door detection and silent movement when alone. They share high-elf languages and add +1 to the initial Intelligence roll, up to 19.

Wood (sylvan) elves have similar elven traits, gain +1 initial Strength (maximum 18) and −1 initial Intelligence. Their starting languages are elvish, common, treant and the tongue of woodland mammals; the passage gives them no other starting languages.

Wild elves (grugach) retain standard elven resistance, weapon bonuses, infravision, silent movement and door detection. They gain +2 initial Strength (maximum 18), deal with woodland creatures as if animal friendship were in effect, and set pits, snares and natural traps with a 90% success chance. Most speak only elvish, though a player character may also know some common.

The UA p.7 class table permits gray elves to be cavaliers, clerics, druids, fighters, rangers, magic-users or thieves (including acrobats and assassins); wood elves have those choices except cavalier; wild elves can be druids, fighters or thieves (including acrobats and assassins). Wild elf multiclassing is restricted to fighter/thief.
These are the UA class choices; ability requirements, multiclass rules and the separate UA class-level limits still apply. Do not merge them with the PHB-only class limits.

UA level-limit table conventions: use Wisdom for cleric/druid, Strength for fighter/ranger/assassin, Intelligence for magic-user, and Dexterity for thief; additional ability requirements appear in footnotes. U means unlimited for the appropriate race/class, subject to the highest level attainable by the class. Below the first score shown, use the lowest listed level; scores above the table do not raise its maximum. If single-classed and that class is an available multiclass choice for the character, the limit may be exceeded by 2. Class eligibility still applies.
UA elf cleric (all except dark elves): Wisdom 12–15: 7; 16: 8; 17: 9; 18: 10; 19: 11; 20–21: 12. Wild elves are not eligible for cleric under UA p.7.
UA elf druid: wild elf Wisdom 12–17: 10; 18: 11; 19: 12; 20: 14, each requiring Charisma 18; 21: 17 requiring Charisma 19. Other elves: U, where class-eligible.

UA elf fighter: Strength 12–17 gives gray/high 5, wild 7, wood 6; 18 gives 6/8/7; 18/75 gives 7/8/8; 18/90 gives 8/10/9; 18/99 gives 9/11/10; 18/00 gives 10/12/11; 19 gives 11/13/12; 20 gives 11/13/14. Values in each group are gray/high, wild, wood respectively.
UA elf magic-user: Intelligence 17–18 gives gray 11 and wood 9; 19 gives 12/10; 20 gives 13/11; 21 gives 15/13; 22 gives 18/13. Wild elves cannot be magic-users under UA p.7.

UA elf thief is U. UA elf assassin: Strength 18, 18/01, 18/51 or 18/76 gives level 10; 18/99 gives 11 with Intelligence 18 and Wisdom 19; 18/00, 19 or 20 gives 12 with Intelligence 19 or Wisdom 19. Apply eligibility separately.

UA elf ranger: Strength 18 gives level 6; 18/01 gives 7 with Intelligence 15 and Wisdom 15, or 8 if both exceed 15; 18/51 gives 9 with Intelligence and Wisdom 16; 18/76, 18/99 or 18/00 gives 10 with Intelligence and Wisdom 17; 19 gives 12 and 20 gives 14, both requiring Intelligence and Wisdom 18. Wild elves cannot be rangers under UA p.7.

oldValue: The legend distinguishes preference, goodwill, tolerance, neutrality, antipathy and hatred.
For elves reacting to a half-elf, use the more negative of the half-elf reaction or the reaction to the elven ancestor's race.
These are encounter and social-context guidelines, not automatic decisions for every individual.
newValue: Read the row as the reacting race and the column as the race observed. The entries are general attitudes and need not be reciprocal.
Legend: P preferred; G goodwill; T tolerated; N neutral (possibly suspicious); A antipathy; H strong hatred.

For reactions of races other than elves, use the half-elf column. An elf reacting to a half-elf uses whichever is more negative: its half-elf reaction or its reaction to a full-blooded elf of the half-elf’s nonhuman ancestor’s race.
